item.title: SEBI: Foreign portfolio investors allowed in physically settled non-agricultural commodity derivatives
item.description:
SEBI · Circular · HO/47/16/13(17)2026-MRD-POD1/I/26650/2026

Effective 2027-06-01.

Who it covers: Foreign portfolio investors, commodity exchanges, clearing corporations and their members.

  • FPIs may trade physically settled non-agricultural commodity derivatives, with safeguards.
  • An FPI cannot take fresh positions in the three trading days before the tender period; positions left open pass to its designated trading or clearing member.
  • In force from 01-06-2027; exchanges and clearing corporations amend their rules before then.

Official source

item.title: RBI: Three payment Directions: card-based transactions, cash withdrawal at ATMs and PoS, and White Label ATM operators
item.description:
RBI · Directions

  • RBI issued three Directions on 27-11-2026: Digital Payments (Card-based transaction) Directions, Cash Withdrawal Transactions through ATMs and PoS Directions, and White Label ATM Operators Directions, all 2026.
  • The Directions are listed on RBI's Master Directions page; read each text for the operative requirements and commencement.

item.title: SEBI: Simplification of client on-boarding and rationalisation of risk management framework at KYC Registration Agencies
item.description:
SEBI · Circular

Effective 2026-12-24.

Who it covers: All SEBI-registered intermediaries that on-board clients, and KYC Registration Agencies.

  • Common supplementary client information (such as income range, FATCA/CRS details, PEP status and occupation) is centralised at the KRA, along with CKYC ID, DIGIPIN and the expiry date of the officially valid document.
  • Intermediaries upload the specified KYC information to the KRA within three working days of completing KYC.
  • In force from 24-12-2026; KRAs issue an operating procedure within 30 days.

Official source

item.description:

Who it covers: Commodity exchanges, clearing corporations and members serving Farmer Producer Organisations.

item.description:
IRDAI · Order · IRDAI/PP&GR/ORD/MISC/155/11/2026

item.title: IFSC: Market makers get up to two more working days to deliver in specified products
item.description:
IFSC · Circular

Effective 2026-11-25.

Who it covers: IFSC stock exchanges, clearing corporations and market makers.

  • The Master Circular for exchanges and clearing corporations is amended: market makers in specified products may deliver within up to two additional working days.

item.title: IFSC: All IFSC entities to act on CERT-In advisories and vulnerability notes
item.description:
IFSC · Circular · IFSCA circular dated 25-11-2026

Effective 2026-11-25.

Who it covers: All regulated entities, including systems run for them by the parent or third parties.

  • Comply with CERT-In advisories and vulnerability notes, including for systems run by the parent or vendors.
  • Set up a tracking mechanism within 30 days; assessment and patching duties apply to advisories issued from 25-11-2026.
  • Reminds entities that CERT-In's own directions (6-hour incident reporting, 180-day logs) apply independently.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: Higher margin on shares with high promoter and non-promoter encumbrance: list revised
item.description:
Exchanges · Exchange circular · NSE/SURV/77601

Effective 2026-11-30.

Who it covers: Trading members and investors in the listed shares; lenders against those shares.

  • Shares that meet the encumbrance criteria attract a minimum 75% margin in the equity and equity derivatives segments from 30-11-2026.
  • The circular lists shares added to, and moved out of, the framework. BSE issued a matching notice.
  • Inclusion is a surveillance measure and not an adverse finding against the company.

Official source

item.title: IRDAI: Two study groups on transparency and accountability in health insurance claims
item.description:
IRDAI · Press release

Who it covers: Health insurers and general insurers writing health business.

  • The IAC Sub-Committee on Health Insurance has formed two study groups: one on claims and grievance metrics and standard reason codes for rejections and deductions, the other on real-time tracking of the claim journey.
  • Both are to report by 26-12-2026. No rule has changed yet.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: Advisory against publishing grey market premium for upcoming IPOs
item.description:
SEBI · Press release

Who it covers: Registered intermediaries, issuers and investors.

  • SEBI states that the pre-listing or "grey market" premium is unregulated and unreliable.
  • Registered intermediaries are told not to publish or circulate grey market premium for upcoming public issues.

Official source

item.title: RBI: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Securitisation Transactions) Amendment Directions, 2026
item.description:
RBI · Amendment Directions · RBI/2026-27/306; DOR.STR.REC.258/21-04-177/2026-27

Effective 2027-04-01.

Who it covers: NBFCs covered by para 3 of the NBFC Securitisation Transactions Directions 2025: NBFC-D, NBFC-ICC, NBFC-Factor, NBFC-MFI, NBFC-IFC, IDF-NBFC and HFCs (para 3(vii)), all layers. Outside para 3: CICs, MGCs, NBFC-P2P, NBFC-AA, NOFHCs, SPDs and Type I NBFCs, so an Upper Layer CIC is not covered as originator. Direct assignments of loans fall under the separate Transfer of Loan Exposures Directions and are not affected. The same changes were made on the same day for commercial banks, SFBs and AIFIs (RBI/2026-27/304, 305, 307).

  • para 26 (substituted): the issuance, holding and subsequent transfer of securitisation notes must be in dematerialised form only. The ₹1 crore minimum ticket size applies at issue and at every later transfer. The originator must ensure that its agreement with the SPE requires the SPE to put in place arrangements with entities such as the registrar, depository and stock exchange, "as may be applicable", to secure the minimum ticket size. Proviso: notes with amortisation structures may be traded at amortised value if the ticket size falls below ₹1 crore. Explanation: ticket size is the investment of a single investor.
  • para 27 (substituted): for an offer of securitisation notes to the public, Regulation 21 of the SEBI (Issue and Listing of Securitised Debt Instruments and Security Receipts) Regulations 2008 must be complied with. RBI's own earlier wording (listing "recommended, though not mandatory"; offers to fifty or more persons to be listed) is removed, so the SEBI Regulations now decide what is a public offer.
  • para 27A (new): transactions in notes issued before 01-04-2027 must also comply with paras 26 and 27. There is no grandfathering for older notes.
  • Effective 01-04-2027 (para 3). Press release 2026-2027/1550 says this finalises the draft of 27-07-2026 after comments.

Official source

item.title: RBI: Governor meets MDs and CEOs of select NBFCs, HFCs and industry bodies
item.description:
RBI · Meeting (press release) · Press Release 2026-2027/1554

Who it covers: Select NBFCs (including Government NBFCs), HFCs and MFIs. Sa-Dhan, MFIN and FIDC took part, and the NHB MD & CEO attended. No new directions were issued.

  • The Governor stressed responsible and sustainable credit growth, fair recovery practices, use of CKYCR for onboarding, and a comprehensive, risk-based approach to cyber and IT risk.

Official source

item.title: RBI: Draft Amendment Directions on 'Preventive Safeguards for Electronic Banking Transactions (EBTs)'
item.description:
RBI · Draft Amendment Directions (for comment) · Press Release 2026-2027/1548

Who it covers: Seven drafts amending the Responsible Business Conduct Directions for commercial banks, SFBs, payments banks, LABs, RRBs, UCBs and RCBs. No NBFC or HFC draft. Comments due by 14-12-2026.

  • Seven draft amendments to the banks' Responsible Business Conduct Directions. Per the press release, they aim to give customers greater control over how and how far their digital payment channels can be used, and to widen the definition of "negligence by a bank" in the 24-06-2026 customer-liability amendment.
  • The press release does not describe the detailed proposals; they are in the seven draft documents.

Official source

item.title: IRDAI: Re-constitution of the Advisory Committee to review the performance of the Insurance Ombudsman system
item.description:
IRDAI · Order · IRDAI/PP&GR/ORD/MISC/154/11/2026

Effective 2026-11-23.

Who it covers: IRDAI and the Insurance Ombudsman system.

  • Re-constitutes the committee under rule 19(1) of the Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 for two years.
  • It meets at least twice a year and reports every year.

Official source

item.title: IRDAI: Expert Committee to examine responses to the consultation paper on Recalibrating Economics of Insurance Distribution
item.description:
IRDAI · Order · IRDAI/INT/ORD/MISC/157/11/2026

Effective 2026-11-23.

Who it covers: Insurers and all distribution channels.

  • Sets up an expert committee to review the responses (about 2.18 lakh answers from over 13,000 respondents) to the 23-09-2026 consultation paper and recommend refinements.
  • No rule has changed yet.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: Proposal to strengthen governance of market infrastructure institutions
item.description:
SEBI · Consultation paper

Who it covers: Stock exchanges, clearing corporations and depositories.

  • Proposals for public interest directors: maximum age to fall from 75 to 70; at most two terms of three years across all such institutions, down from three; membership of at most four statutory committees.
  • Changes are also proposed to the tenure of managing directors and executive directors.
  • Comments are due by 11-12-2026. SEBI issued a clarification on media reports about the paper on 27-11-2026.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: Proposal to review the additional disclosure framework for foreign portfolio investors
item.description:
SEBI · Consultation paper

Who it covers: Foreign portfolio investors, designated depository participants and custodians.

  • SEBI proposes changes to the rules that require granular ownership disclosures from FPIs with concentrated or large Indian equity holdings.
  • Comments are due by 11-12-2026.

Official source

item.title: RBI: RBI imposes monetary penalty on an NBFC
item.description:
RBI · Enforcement (press release) · Press Release 2026-2027/1537 (order dated 17-11-2026)

Who it covers: Another lender (described as an NBFC in secondary sources). It is a routine enforcement order and creates no new rule.

  • Penalty of ₹7.50 lakh by order of 17-11-2026, under RBI Act s.58G(1)(b) read with s.58B(5)(aa), following a statutory inspection of the position as on 31-03-2026.
  • Findings: the company failed to obtain PAN (or its e-document) or Form 60 when establishing account-based relationships, and failed to escalate partly or wholly rejected complaints to the Internal Ombudsman within the prescribed time. RBI cites its KYC and Internal Ombudsman directions without paragraph numbers.

Official source

item.title: IRDAI: Penalty on a standalone health insurer for claim repudiations and deductions
item.description:
IRDAI · Enforcement order (penalty) · IRDAI/E&C/ORD/MISC/153/11/2026

Effective 2026-11-20.

Who it covers: The health insurer named in the order. The rules applied are unchanged.

  • Rs 2 crore penalty under s. 102 of the Insurance Act for repudiating claims on untenable grounds and making deductions not supported by policy terms.
  • Breaches found of regulations 27(v) and 33(d) of the Health Insurance Regulations 2016 and regulation 21(3) of the TPA Regulations; warnings and directions also issued.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: Retail algorithmic trading: compliance reminder on static IP use
item.description:
Exchanges · Exchange circular · NSE/INSP/77559

Who it covers: Trading members, algorithm providers and clients using algorithmic trading.

  • Under the retail algo framework in force from 01-04-2026, strategies run on the broker's servers; only a "tech-savvy" client may host its own algorithm, on a static IP.
  • The exchange has received complaints that some empanelled algorithm providers misuse the static IP facility, and reminds members to comply. BSE issued a matching notice.

Official source

item.title: Other laws: High-Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat begins stakeholder consultations
item.description:
Other laws · Press release

Who it covers: Banks and other financial institutions.

  • The committee set up to recommend reforms to the banking sector has started consulting stakeholders.
  • No change in law yet.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: Review of margin framework for commodity derivatives
item.description:
SEBI · Circular

Effective 2026-12-01.

Who it covers: Commodity exchanges, clearing corporations and their members.

  • Minimum initial margin is set at 6%, 8% or 10% according to the commodity's volatility category, for agricultural and non-agricultural commodities.
  • The margin period of risk is two days for the first two categories and three days for the most volatile.
  • In force from 01-12-2026 and valid for one year.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: Sub-group formed to review parts of the ICDR Regulations
item.description:
SEBI · Press release

Who it covers: Issuers, merchant bankers and investors in public and rights issues.

  • A sub-group of the Primary Market Advisory Committee will review Chapters II, IIA, IV, V and VI of the ICDR Regulations, 2018.
  • No rule changes yet; proposals would follow as a consultation paper.

Official source

item.title: RBI: 13 NBFCs and one HFC surrender their registrations
item.description:
RBI · Enforcement (press release) · Press Release 2026-2027/1500

Who it covers: The entities named in the press release.

  • RBI cancelled the registrations on surrender: six entities exited the non-banking financial business, five met the criteria for unregistered Type I status, and three ceased to exist as legal entities.
  • The HFC registration was cancelled under section 29A of the National Housing Bank Act.

Official source

item.title: RBI: Certificates of Registration of 49 NBFCs cancelled
item.description:
RBI · Enforcement (press release) · Press Release 2026-2027/1501

Who it covers: The NBFCs named in the press release; lenders and partners dealing with them.

  • RBI cancelled the registration of 49 NBFCs under section 45-IA(6) of the RBI Act, by orders passed in October 2026.
  • A separate release of 09-11-2026 announced one more cancellation.
  • An entity whose registration is cancelled cannot carry on the business of a non-banking financial institution.

Official source

item.title: RBI: Monetary penalty on a prepaid payment instrument issuer
item.description:
RBI · Enforcement (press release) · Press Release 2026-2027/1496

Who it covers: A non-bank prepaid payment instrument issuer.

  • Penalty of ₹9.00 lakh under section 30 of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, by order dated 06-11-2026.
  • Findings: fund transfers by wallet holders to beneficiaries that were not pre-registered went beyond the permitted limit, and frauds were not reported to RBI in time.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Commodity trading notified as a financial service, and commodity trading contracts as a financial product
item.description:
IFSC · Notification · S.O. 6195(E) and S.O. 6196(E)

Effective 2026-11-13.

Who it covers: Entities wishing to set up commodity trading operations in the IFSC.

  • The Central Government notified "commodity trading" as a financial service and "commodity trading contract" as a financial product under section 3 of the IFSCA Act, 2019.
  • This lets IFSCA frame rules for commodity trading entities in the IFSC.

Official source

item.title: IBC: Disciplinary orders: three insolvency professionals suspended for two years each
item.description:
IBC · Enforcement order

Who it covers: Insolvency professionals; creditors' committees that appoint them.

  • The IBBI Disciplinary Committee suspended the registration of three insolvency professionals for two years each, by orders of 03-11-2026, 12-11-2026 and 13-11-2026.
  • Each order says the professional is not eligible to continue existing assignments (section 206), so a replacement must be appointed under the procedure for that process.
  • A fourth order of 09-11-2026 concerned the conduct of a liquidation, including valuation and a scheme placed without secured creditors' consent.

Official source

item.title: DPDP: Consent Manager registration opens under the DPDP Act
item.description:
DPDP · Commencement · s. 6(9) and s. 27(1)(d) of the Act; rule 4 of the DPDP Rules, 2025

Effective 2026-11-13.

Who it covers: Companies that want to register as Consent Managers, and Data Fiduciaries that plan to accept consent through them.

  • Rule 4 and the First Schedule apply from 13-11-2026: an Indian company with net worth of at least Rs 2 crore and an independently certified platform may apply to the Board.
  • The Board may inquire into a breach of a Consent Manager's registration conditions (s. 27(1)(d)).
  • The duties of Data Fiduciaries on notice, consent, security and breaches still start on 13-05-2027.

Official source

item.title: NHB: Arbitrators must be independent; report action to NHB
item.description:
NHB · Advisory · RBI DoR.CO.BCG(MCS).No.S6464/01.01.008/2026-27

Effective 2026-11-12.

Who it covers: Banks and NBFCs, including HFCs.

  • After a Delhi High Court order of 30-09-2026, RBI cautioned lenders against appointing the same arbitrators unilaterally across many disputes.
  • Arbitrators are to be appointed only in line with the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 and court rulings on independence and neutrality.
  • HFCs report the action taken to NHB.

Official source

item.title: Other laws: FIU-IND order against a virtual digital asset platform under PMLA section 13
item.description:
Other laws · Order · Order No. 11/DIR/FIU-IND/2026

Who it covers: Reporting entities under the PMLA, especially virtual digital asset service providers.

  • The Director, FIU-IND passed an order under section 13 of the PMLA against a virtual digital asset service provider.
  • See the order for the findings and the penalty.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Registration of IFSC insurance offices stays valid on payment of the annual fee
item.description:
IFSC · Circular

Effective 2026-11-12.

Who it covers: IFSC Insurance Offices.

  • The certificate of registration of an IFSC Insurance Office continues to be valid as long as the annual fee is paid; no periodic renewal is needed.
  • This aligns with the Insurance Act as amended in 2025.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Bullion exchange and clearing corporation: quarterly non-compliance report
item.description:
IFSC · Circular

Effective 2026-11-12.

Who it covers: The bullion exchange and bullion clearing corporation in the IFSC.

  • Prescribes the format for reporting non-compliance under regulation 31 of the Bullion Market Regulations, 2025.
  • The report is due within 45 days of each quarter end; a nil report must be filed.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: FATCA and CRS reporting revised under the Income-Tax Act, 2025 and Income-Tax Rules, 2026
item.description:
SEBI · Circular

Effective 2026-11-11.

Who it covers: Registered intermediaries that are Reporting Financial Institutions.

  • Reporting and due diligence now follow s. 508 of the Income-Tax Act, 2025 and rules 238 to 240 and Form 166 of the Income-Tax Rules, 2026.
  • Self-certification, controlling person and account classification systems must capture the new fields; FATCA/CRS certifications are uploaded to the KRA.

Official source

item.title: RBI: RBI updates its FAQs "All you wanted to know about NBFCs"
item.description:
RBI · FAQs (updated)

Who it covers: All NBFCs and the public.

  • RBI refreshed its general FAQ page on NBFCs on 11-11-2026.
  • FAQs explain the rules and do not change them.

Official source

item.title: RBI: Domestic Money Transfer Directions, 2026
item.description:
RBI · Directions · RBI/DPSS/2026-27/476

Effective 2026-11-11.

Who it covers: Banks, authorised payment system operators and participants offering domestic money transfer. Card-to-card transfers are excluded.

  • Cash pay-out is capped at ₹10,000 per transaction and ₹25,000 a month per beneficiary; walk-in customers may remit up to ₹50,000 by NEFT.
  • Cash-based remittance through business correspondents and ATMs is capped at ₹5,000 per transaction and ₹25,000 a month per remitter.
  • The remitter is registered using a verified mobile number and a self-certified officially valid document, and every transaction needs an additional factor of authentication.
  • The IMPS or NEFT message must carry the remitter's details and an identifier marking it as a cash-based remittance.
  • The circulars of 05-10-2011 and 24-07-2024 are repealed.

Official source

item.title: Other laws: Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units and Stand-Up India continued to 31-03-2031
item.description:
Other laws · Cabinet decision

Who it covers: Banks, NBFCs and micro-finance institutions lending under the Mudra scheme and Stand-Up India.

  • The Cabinet approved the Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units for five more years, to 31-03-2031, with a corpus of ₹5,000 crore to guarantee Mudra loans.
  • Stand-Up India is also continued to 31-03-2031, with a credit guarantee corpus of ₹4,111 crore, aiming at 2.5 lakh more women and SC/ST entrepreneurs.

Official source

item.title: Companies Act: Draft changes to Schedule VII and the CSR Policy Rules
item.description:
Companies Act · Draft rules (for comment)

Who it covers: Companies covered by section 135 (corporate social responsibility).

  • The Ministry published draft amendments to Schedule VII of the Companies Act and to the CSR Policy Rules for comment.
  • See the draft for the proposed changes and the last date for comments.

Official source

item.title: IRDAI: Working Groups on convergence of the Risk Based Capital framework with Ind AS
item.description:
IRDAI · Order · IRDAI/RBC/ORD/MISC/150/11/2026

Effective 2026-11-10.

Who it covers: All insurers.

  • Sets up Life and Non-Life working groups so that Ind AS financial statements become the starting point for RBC, with defined prudential adjustments.
  • No rule has changed yet.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Two consultations: Financial Solicitation Professionals and model portfolios by research entities
item.description:
IFSC · Consultation paper

Who it covers: Capital market intermediaries, fund managers, distributors and research entities in the IFSC.

  • IFSCA proposes disclosure-based guidelines for engaging Financial Solicitation Professionals, and drops the idea of separate Financial Advisers regulations.
  • A second paper proposes to let research entities offer model portfolios.
  • Comments on both are due by 30-11-2026.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: Investment advisers must confirm their websites, apps and social media handles on the exchange portal
item.description:
Exchanges · Exchange notice · BSE Notice No. 20261109-1

Who it covers: Registered investment advisers (a matching notice covers research analysts).

  • BSE opened a "Digital Platform" facility on its portal for advisers to submit or correct details of the websites, mobile apps and social media handles they use.
  • Details already filed are pre-filled; advisers verify and submit.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: SEBI (Settlement of Administrative and Civil Proceedings) Regulations, 2026 in force
item.description:
SEBI · Regulations · SEBI/LAD-DOP/2026/318

Effective 2026-11-07.

Who it covers: Anyone facing or likely to face SEBI proceedings.

  • Replace the Settlement Proceedings Regulations, 2018.
  • Settlement notices before a show cause notice, a formula-based settlement amount, and fast track settlement for delayed or wrong-format disclosures.
  • Applications within 90 days of a show cause notice; pending cases not settled under the 2018 rules may apply within 90 days at a 20% higher amount.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: Consultation paper: AML/CFT certification for Principal Officers of intermediaries
item.description:
SEBI · Consultation paper

Who it covers: All intermediaries registered under s. 12 of the SEBI Act.

  • Proposes a mandatory AML/CFT certification for the Principal Officer responsible for PMLA compliance.
  • No rule has changed yet.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: Comprehensive FAQs on the Insider Trading Regulations
item.description:
SEBI · FAQs

Who it covers: Listed companies, their designated persons, intermediaries and fiduciaries.

  • SEBI published a consolidated set of FAQs on the Prohibition of Insider Trading Regulations, 2015.
  • FAQs give SEBI's view and do not amend the regulations.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: Framework for net settlement of funds for mutual fund cash market transactions
item.description:
SEBI · Circular

Effective 2027-04-01.

Who it covers: Mutual funds, custodians, stock brokers and clearing corporations.

  • Funds for outright transactions in the cash segment may be settled net at the level of each scheme; securities still settle gross.
  • No netting across schemes. In force from 01-04-2027.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: Currency derivatives: single USD 5 million limit without establishing underlying exposure
item.description:
SEBI · Circular

Effective 2026-11-05.

Who it covers: Stock exchanges, clearing corporations, members and clients trading exchange-traded currency derivatives.

  • Domestic clients and foreign portfolio investors may take positions up to USD 5 million (notional, outstanding at any time), across all rupee currency pairs and all exchanges together, without having to establish that an underlying exposure exists.
  • Follows RBI's A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 25 of 10-10-2026.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: Review of the framework for Accredited Investors
item.description:
SEBI · Circular

Effective 2026-11-05.

Who it covers: AIF managers, SIF AMCs and portfolio managers, and their investors.

  • Managers may determine and record an investor's accredited status themselves, valid for three years and recognised across the same group.
  • Securities market exposure qualifies: at least Rs 5 crore for individuals, HUFs, family trusts and sole proprietorships, and Rs 20 crore for bodies corporate and other trusts.

Official source

item.title: RBI: Draft consolidated Priority Sector Lending Directions for banks
item.description:
RBI · Draft Directions (for comment) · Press Release 2026-2027/1447

Who it covers: Commercial banks, small finance banks, local area banks, regional rural banks and urban co-operative banks.

  • RBI published five draft Priority Sector Lending (Targets and Classification) Directions that consolidate the existing instructions for each type of bank.
  • Comments closed on 26-11-2026.

Official source

item.title: RBI: Master Directions on Cyber Resilience and Digital Payment Security Controls for non-bank Payment System Operators
item.description:
RBI · Directions · RBI/DPSS/2026-27/475

Effective 2026-11-05.

Who it covers: Non-bank payment system operators: in force on issue for large and medium operators, and from 01-04-2028 for small operators.

  • Consolidates the 2024 Master Directions with the earlier circulars on ATM switch application service providers and system-audit scope.
  • A Board sub-committee reviews cyber risk every quarter; the information-security policy is reviewed every year.
  • Unusual incidents such as cyber-attacks and outages of critical systems are reported to RBI within six hours of detection; audit logs are kept for five years.
  • The annual System Audit Report is filed within two months of the financial year end.
  • Operators must make sure the unregulated entities in their payment chain follow the controls.
  • The Master Direction on Payment Aggregators was updated on 11-11-2026 to refer to these Directions.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: Review of KYC process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
item.description:
SEBI · Circular

Effective 2026-12-03.

Who it covers: Intermediaries on-boarding NRI, OCI and foreign national individual clients.

  • Digital KYC is allowed for individual clients located in FATF-compliant countries, without being in India.
  • Intermediaries may rely on KYC by another SEBI or financial sector regulated entity through KRA or CKYCRR records.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: Working group to review the Innovators Growth Platform
item.description:
SEBI · Press release

Who it covers: Start-ups, their investors and merchant bankers.

  • SEBI set up a working group to review the framework for listing on the Innovators Growth Platform.
  • No rule changes yet.

Official source

item.title: Other laws: CERT-In guidelines on auditing the security of AI systems
item.description:
Other laws · Guidelines · CISG-2026-04

Who it covers: Organisations that build or deploy AI systems, and CERT-In empanelled auditors.

  • CERT-In published Artificial Intelligence (AI) Security Auditing Guidelines on 04-11-2026.
  • No new Directions under section 70B of the IT Act were issued in November.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Reporting norms for TechFin and ancillary service providers, global in-house centres and book-keeping firms
item.description:
IFSC · Circular

Effective 2026-11-04.

Who it covers: TechFin and ancillary service providers, Global In-House Centres, and book-keeping, accounting, taxation and financial crime compliance service providers.

  • Monthly and quarterly reports are due by the 10th of the following month.
  • Anti-money laundering reports are half-yearly; the annual report is due by 31 May and audited financial statements by 30 September.
  • Material changes are reported within 30 days.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: No tax deducted at source on dividends between IFSC aircraft-leasing units
item.description:
IFSC · Notification · S.O. 6016(E)

Who it covers: Aircraft-leasing units in the IFSC.

  • The Central Board of Direct Taxes notified that no tax is deducted at source on dividends paid by one IFSC aircraft-leasing unit to another, on a declaration in the prescribed form.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Leasing of GPUs and connected data-centre equipment notified as a financial product
item.description:
IFSC · Notification · IFSCA/GN/2026/017

Effective 2026-10-29.

Who it covers: Finance companies and lessors in the IFSC.

  • Operating leases, and hybrids of operating and financial leases, of graphics processing units and connected data-centre equipment are a financial product in the IFSC.
  • The notification is dated 22-10-2026 and was published in the Gazette on 29-10-2026; IFSCA listed it on 04-11-2026.

Official source

item.title: IRDAI: Exposure Draft: IRDAI (Subsidiary Instructions and Consultative Committees) Regulations, 2026
item.description:
IRDAI · Exposure draft (for comment)

Who it covers: All regulated entities.

  • Proposes regulations under the new ss. 114B and 114C of the Insurance Act (inserted by the SBSR Act 2025) on the scope of subsidiary instructions, consultation, urgent instructions, review and withdrawal, and Consultative Committees.
  • Comments were due by 23-11-2026.

Official source
